facts.text: Residual risk is the risk remaining after all protective measures are in place; ALARP is the principle that risk must be reduced until the cost of further reduction would be grossly out of proportion to the benefit gained.
facts.quote: Residual risk is the risk that remains after all the protective measures are in place, and ALARP is the principle that risk must be reduced until the cost of reducing it further would be grossly out of proportion to the benefit gained.

facts.text: Every safety case ends with a statement of residual risk and a named person or board accepting that risk.
facts.quote: every safety case ends with a statement of it and a named person or board accepting it.

facts.text: ISO 12100 defines residual risk as the risk remaining after protective measures have been taken.
facts.quote: ISO 12100 defines it as the risk remaining after protective measures have been taken.

facts.text: ALARP comes from British health and safety law, whose duty is to reduce risk "so far as is reasonably practicable"; the same wording appears in Australian workplace law.
facts.quote: ALARP comes from British health and safety law, where the duty is to reduce risk "so far as is reasonably practicable", and the same wording appears in Australian workplace law

facts.text: Australia's model regulation on powered mobile plant requires collision risk to be controlled so far as reasonably practicable.
facts.quote: Australia's model regulation on powered mobile plant requires collision risk to be controlled so far as reasonably practicable [Chapter 3].

facts.text: Under ALARP, a risk-reduction measure is required unless its cost in money, time or trouble is grossly disproportionate to the risk reduction it brings.
facts.quote: a measure is required unless its cost in money, time or trouble is grossly disproportionate to the risk reduction it brings.

facts.text: The ALARP proportionality test is a judgment rather than a formula, making the record of the reasoning important.
facts.quote: It is a judgment, not a formula, which is why the record of the reasoning matters.

facts.text: The booklet frames the safety evidence chain as ending in a residual risk decision.
facts.quote: The booklet frames the evidence chain as ending in a "residual risk decision" [Chapter 13].

facts.text: The evidence package an assessor expects ends with a residual-risk statement and limitations specifying what the simulation evidence does not establish.
facts.quote: The package an assessor expects ends with a residual-risk statement and limitations: what the simulation evidence does not establish [Chapter 10].

facts.text: Every reviewer should be shown who has authority to accept the remaining uncertainty in the collision mitigation program.
facts.quote: Every reviewer should see who has authority to accept the remaining uncertainty [Chapter 13]

facts.text: The proposed top-level safety claim for the collision mitigation program includes explicitly bounded residual uncertainty.
facts.quote: the proposed top-level claim speaks of "explicitly bounded residual uncertainty" [Chapter 12].

facts.text: The collision mitigation program's residual risk includes two unusual parts: risk added by unnecessary stops and uncertainty remaining from reliance on simulation.
facts.quote: For this program the residual risk has two unusual parts: the risk the function adds through unnecessary stops, and the uncertainty left by relying on simulation.

facts.text: Absence of failures in testing does not prove zero risk for the collision mitigation program.
facts.quote: Absence of failures in testing is not proof of zero risk [Chapter 1].

facts.text: Pressure to declare residual risk acceptable grows as the collision mitigation program's deadline approaches.
facts.quote: As a deadline approaches, pressure grows to declare the residual risk acceptable.

facts.text: The collision mitigation program's launch decision should be tied to unresolved safety evidence rather than calendar pressure.
facts.quote: The booklet says the launch decision should be tied to unresolved safety evidence rather than to calendar pressure [Chapter 13].
